title: Lipschitz convex finite-sum minimization with ball-restricted exact component values
summary: Finite-population exact component-value queries are restricted to the feasible Euclidean ball. The expected-error frontier explicitly retains dimension, population size, and accuracy.

description_paragraphs: Minimize $F(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x)$ over the public Euclidean ball $X=B_2(0,R)$ using selected component values.
task.formulation: Minimize $F(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x)$ over the public Euclidean ball $X=B_2(0,R)$ using selected component values.

description_paragraphs: Each fixed client function $f_i:X\to\mathbb R$ is finite, convex, and $L$-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm. Neither smoothness nor a shared minimizer is assumed. No definition or regularity outside $X$ is required. Boundary minimizers are permitted.
The complete tuple $(f_1,\ldots,f_N)$ is fixed before private randomization. Revisiting a client accesses the same function rather than a fresh stochastic loss.

assumptions.description: Each fixed client function $f_i:X\to\mathbb R$ is finite, convex, and $L$-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm. Neither smoothness nor a shared minimizer is assumed. No definition or regularity outside $X$ is required. Boundary minimizers are permitted.

assumptions.description: The complete tuple $(f_1,\ldots,f_N)$ is fixed before private randomization. Revisiting a client accesses the same function rather than a fresh stochastic loss.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

description_paragraphs: One call selects $(i,x)\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\times X$ and returns exactly one scalar $f_i(x)$. Both the client and the feasible point may be selected adaptively. Off-domain queries are not legal.

The public inputs are $d,N,L,R,\varepsilon$. A complete average, a group average, or a two-point difference must be computed from its actual component calls; no aggregate-value interface is supplied for free.
oracle.operation: One call selects $(i,x)\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\times X$ and returns exactly one scalar $f_i(x)$. Both the client and the feasible point may be selected adaptively. description_paragraphs: Return a measurable feasible $\widehat x\in X$, which need not have been queried.
output.feasibility: Return a measurable feasible $\widehat x\in X$, which need not have been queried.

description_paragraphs: The loss is $F(\widehat x)-F^\star$, where $F^\star=\min_{x\in X}F(x)$. Only this loss is averaged over the independent private seed.
metric.base_expression: The loss is $F(\widehat x)-F^\star$, where $F^\star=\min_{x\in X}F(x)$. Only this loss is averaged over the independent private seed.

description_paragraphs: Each selected scalar component value costs one call. The cap holds for every fixed seed and every possible scalar history, including initialization and verification. Internal computation, storage, projection, and operations on public domain geometry are uncharged. Communication rounds are not a resource of this comparison.

description_paragraphs: Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.
Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.
The expectation is over the algorithmic seed after fixing all client functions. Every query and the output must be feasible, and the total component-value count is capped on every execution.
